In Islamic tradition, Bina is associated with building houses, or rebuilding and improving one's life. It symbolizes the creation of something new, the rebuilding of something old, and the improvement of one's self. The name Bina is also associated with the concept of self-improvement and personal development.

historical_references.reference: Bina was the name of a major port city in the Persian Gulf during the Sassanid Empire (224-651 AD). It was a crucial trading center and an important military post against the Byzantine and Arab threats.
historical_references.context: Major port city and military post

historical_references.reference: Bina was also the name of a medieval Islamic city in present-day Pakistan, capital of the Bhakkar State in the Indus Valley Civilization (3300-1300 BC). It was a significant commercial and cultural center during the Islamic Golden Age (750-1258 AD).
